claims.text: The starting WC powder has an average particle size of 0.4 µm.
The WC-CoNiFe system is prepared with carbon contents in the range 5.44–5.50 wt%.
Planetary ball milling is used before consolidation and sintering.
Low-pressure sintering of WC-CoNiFe can be conducted under 5.0 MPa argon at 1450 °C.
Spark Plasma Sintering at 1450 °C will cause rapid densification while minimizing the available time for atomic diffusion.
A carbon content of 5.46 wt% and a sintering temperature of 1450 °C provide the optimal reported properties for WC-10CoNiFe.
WC-10CoNiFe has a finer grain size of 0.261 µm than the 0.294 µm grain size of optimally processed WC-10Co.
The Co-Ni-Fe binder remains a refined, single-phase FCC solid solution after processing.
The Co-Ni-Fe binder suppresses WC dissolution and reprecipitation and concentrates grain-growth inhibitors at WC/binder interfaces.
The selected binder and carbon content prevent brittle eta phases and graphite from forming.
High lattice distortion and sluggish diffusion in the multi-principal-element binder retard WC dissolution and subsequent reprecipitation.
Rapid SPS processing further limits WC grain growth relative to conventional sintering.
A carbon content of 5.46 wt% thermodynamically stabilizes WC without detrimental secondary phases.
The processed WC-CoNiFe material will have hardness greater than 1765 HV.
The processed WC-CoNiFe material will have transverse rupture strength approaching or exceeding 2999 MPa.
The Co-Ni-Fe binder will form a stable protective oxide scale and preserve material integrity above 1000 °C.
WC-CoNiFe will have superior aqueous-corrosion resistance compared with WC-10Co.
The WC-10Co baseline is optimally processed at 5.48 wt% carbon and 1410 °C and has a grain size of 0.294 µm.
Keeping carbon within 5.44–5.50 wt% prevents eta-phase formation.
Above 1500 °C, accelerated diffusion causes significant grain coarsening that negates the refinement effect of the Co-Ni-Fe binder.

contradictions.description: The framing suggests a hardness advantage over conventional WC-Co, but the cited values reported in the uncertainty context are 1765 HV for WC-CoNiFe versus 1853 HV for WC-Co. The proposed SPS route might change this result, but no evidence is supplied.
